title: Research Bits: Aug. 25
gist: Three university results push computing substrates away from conventional CMOS: MIT built living logic circuits from engineered Pantoea agglomerans bacteria that compute in about eight hours per calculation, Seoul National University and Sungkyunkwan University turned an antiferroelectric device's volatility into a 'forgetting' function that hit 90.4% handwritten-digit accuracy while cutting input data 75%, and Carnegie Mellon and Penn State used high-entropy mixing to convert an insulating metal oxide into a semiconductor with ultra-low thermal conductivity. All three are lab-stage results with no commercial timelines given.

insights.claim: MIT engineered the bacterium Pantoea agglomerans into two transistor types — one switched on by a molecule called OC-6 and one switched off by it — each of which also detects a target molecule OC-12 and emits an output molecule OHC-14 depending on switch state and target presence.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: A working molecular switching primitive means biological computing has moved past single sensors to composable logic — a long-dated but real alternative substrate to silicon sensing.

insights.claim: Circuit topology in MIT's bacterial system is set physically by printing bacterial colonies onto agar plates about 5 millimeters apart, so signals reach only the nearest colony and information flows in one direction — the spacing is the wiring.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Geometry-defined routing removes the need for any fabrication step, which is why this class of computing could be deployed by printing rather than by a fab.
insights.quote: Each colony is printed about 5 millimeters from the nearest one, allowing signals to travel only to the nearest colony, which then relays them to the next one, so information flows only in one direction.
insights.locator: Circuits are created by printing colonies of bacteria

insights.claim: MIT claims that any operation can be built from just five bacterial strains, having demonstrated multi-input, OR, and IMPLY gates from a single transistor whose function depends on its location in the circuit layout.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Functional completeness from five strains is the claim that separates a demo from a platform — it is the assertion to test as this work is replicated.
insights.quote: We’ve built some initial computer architecture components that are commonly used, but any operation can be built with these five strains
insights.locator: We’ve built some initial computer architecture components

insights.claim: MIT's largest demonstrated bacterial circuit contained 24 colonies wired together to add two inputs, with other circuits shown adding signals, processing multiple signals simultaneously, and functioning as a demultiplexer.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: A 24-element ceiling sets the honest scale of the state of the art — orders of magnitude from anything commercial, so treat this as a decade-plus research signal.
insights.quote: The largest circuit contained 24 bacterial colonies wired together to add two inputs.
insights.locator: They also combined the transistors to create more complex circuits

insights.claim: The eight hours these bacterial circuits need per calculation is framed as acceptable rather than disqualifying, because the target application is computational control inside biology — bacteria on plant roots or the plant itself running overnight calculations against a growth-season timescale.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Redefines the benchmark: the competitive set is agricultural sensing and environmental monitoring, not processors — a different and much slower-moving market.
insights.quote: We’re not trying to replace computers, but rather put computational control into biology.
insights.locator: The circuits take about eight hours to perform each calculation

themes.theme: Volatility as a feature: forgetting antiferroelectrics

insights.claim: Seoul National University and Sungkyunkwan University inverted the usual framing of antiferroelectric volatility, treating the material's return to its original state after voltage removal not as a limitation but as a computational 'forgetting' function for time-series data.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: A device property previously counted as a defect becomes the product feature — a pattern worth watching in memory-adjacent materials where 'poor retention' devices may find AI use cases.
insights.quote: we utilized the property of antiferroelectric materials returning to their original state after voltage removal not as a limitation, but as a computational function called ‘forgetting’

insights.claim: The device is a two-terminal stack combining zirconium dioxide with amorphous indium gallium zinc oxide (a-IGZO), where optimizing the IGZO composition produced distinct current differences from minimal state changes.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Both materials are already in production use in DRAM/logic dielectrics and display backplanes, so the fab path is more plausible than for exotic novel-material devices.
insights.locator: The team fabricated a two-terminal device

insights.claim: The optimized antiferroelectric device achieved an on/off current ratio of approximately 890 and separated all 16 combinations of 4-bit inputs into distinct current states.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Resolving 16 states in one two-terminal device is the density argument — it is what would make this cheaper per operation than a CMOS equivalent.
insights.quote: The optimized device demonstrated an on/off current ratio of approximately 890 and successfully distinguished 16 combinations of 4-bit inputs into distinct current states.
insights.locator: The team fabricated a two-terminal device

insights.claim: In handwritten digit recognition the forgetting device reached 90.4% accuracy while reducing input data by 75%, the headline efficiency claim of the work.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: A 4x input-data reduction at ~90% accuracy is the metric to compare against digital preprocessing baselines — the value is bandwidth and energy saved before the classifier runs.
insights.quote: it achieved a 90.4% recognition accuracy while reducing input data by 75%

insights.claim: The stated architectural advantage is collapsing three functions — non-linear transformation, short-term memory, and natural initialization — into a single two-terminal device, with the team's next steps being area reduction and array-level circuit verification toward an on-site edge AI system for voice, biological, and environmental signals.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Array-level verification is the gating milestone; until it lands, single-device results say nothing about whether this can displace digital signal preprocessing.
insights.quote: By simultaneously implementing non-linear transformation, short-term memory, and natural initialization in a single two-terminal device, we have expanded the device options for low-power time-series AI hardware.
insights.locator: We plan to reduce the device area

themes.theme: High-entropy mixing as a materials knob

insights.claim: Carnegie Mellon and Penn State converted an insulating metal oxide into a high-performance semiconductor by mixing manganese, iron, cobalt, nickel, copper, and zinc into a tungsten oxide wolframite framework in a single crystal structure, deliberately creating a state of high configurational entropy.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Turning an insulator into a semiconductor by composition alone widens the candidate materials pool well beyond the silicon/III-V/oxide set currently in play.
insights.quote: a complex mixture of manganese, iron, cobalt, nickel, copper, and zinc into a tungsten oxide framework within a single crystal structure, called wolframite, the researchers intentionally created a state of high configurational entropy

insights.claim: The A6WO4 material's distinguishing result is combining semiconducting transport with exceptionally poor heat conduction — two properties Penn State describes as difficult to achieve together in oxides.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Low thermal conductivity plus electrical conduction is precisely the thermoelectric figure-of-merit recipe — the reason this is a waste-heat-recovery story, not a logic story.
insights.quote: this material combines semiconducting transport with exceptionally poor heat conduction—two properties that are difficult to achieve together in oxides

insights.claim: The researchers position high-entropy mixing as a design knob for engineering electronic and thermal properties simultaneously, not merely a way to create chemical disorder.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: If entropy-driven design generalizes, it becomes a reusable method across materials classes — a research direction to track for thermal-management and thermoelectric materials.
insights.quote: high-entropy mixing is not just a way to create chemical disorder; it can be used as a powerful knob to engineer electronic and thermal properties simultaneously
insights.locator: The measurements show that high-entropy mixing

insights.claim: CMU frames the underlying microscopic mechanisms as a candidate new set of guiding principles for future materials engineering and next-generation device design, with the near-term application anticipated in thermoelectric devices that convert waste heat into electricity.
insights.speaker: Jesse Allen
insights.so_what: Waste-heat conversion is the stated commercial target — relevant to data center and industrial thermal recovery, though at a materials-discovery stage with no timeline given.
insights.quote: This approach activates unique microscopic mechanisms that we believe could serve as a new set of guiding principles for future materials engineering and design of next-generation devices
insights.locator: This approach activates unique microscopic mechanisms
